events.title: ZeroMQ project started
events.summary: Pieter Hintjens and Martin Sustrik started ZeroMQ in May 2007 — a brokerless messaging library with socket-style APIs.
events.about: ZeroMQ (ØMQ) wraps TCP, IPC, and in-process transports behind familiar socket patterns — pub/sub, push/pull, req/rep — without a central message broker. High-frequency trading, distributed systems, and language bindings (Python, C++, Go) use it for fast, lightweight messaging. Example: a PUB socket broadcasts market ticks; SUB sockets filter by topic prefix.

narrative.whyChosen: ZeroMQ brought brokerless, pattern-based messaging to systems that outgrew single-queue brokers.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced modern distributed architectures and proved messaging could live in a library, not only a server.
narrative.problemSolved: Traditional message brokers added latency and operational overhead for simple point-to-point communication.

events.title: Jonathan Schwartz: "innovate, not litigate"
events.quoteText: We decided to innovate, not litigate.
events.summary: Sun CEO Jonathan Schwartz responds to Microsoft's patent threats against Linux — offering Sun's patent portfolio to defend open source instead of suing.
events.about: Press dubbed Microsoft's campaign 'patent terrorism'; Schwartz framed Sun's choice as building better products rather than lawyering rivals. The blog post became a rallying cry during the open-source wars of the 2000s.

narrative.whyChosen: Sun's public line when Microsoft threatened Linux with unspecified patents.
narrative.whyImportant: It contrasted litigation strategy with open-source ecosystem building.
narrative.problemSolved: The Linux community needed corporate allies willing to counter patent FUD.
